title: An endomorphism of a nonzero finite-dimensional space has an eigenvalue
statement: Let $K$ be an algebraically closed field [def-weil-algebraic-closure] and $V$ a nonzero finite-dimensional $K$-vector space [def-weil-finite-dimensional-subspace]. For every $K$-linear endomorphism $A:V\to V$, there is $\alpha\in K$ which is an eigenvalue of $A$, meaning that there exists $z\in V$ with $z\ne0$ and $A(z)=\alpha z$.
